newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty eases on higher Polish rate rise likelyhood.
newsitem.headline: Zloty eases on higher Polish rate rise likelyhood.

text.p: The zloty closed softer against the basket of currencies on foreign sales of Polish paper after the central bank said that the planned size of the 1998 budget deficit increased the likelyhood of a rate rise, dealers said.
They said some foreign players trimmed Polish positions ahead of the potential rate rise depressing the zloty to about 0.6 percent above parity from the opening 1.11/1.02 percent.
But other investors found the low-point an attractive level to buy Polish instruments and pushed the zloty back again to close at 0.73/0.67 percent above the parity rate in busy trade.
The NBP is trying to curb domestic demand by keeping high real interest rates and raising obligatory reserves for banks to avoid a Czech style crisis because of a balooning trade gap.
On the money market the NBP statement boosted bids for one-, two- and three-month deposits, which rose 0.2-0.3 point to 22.40-22.55 percent.

O/N and T/N rates were flat at 23.05/23.45 percent throught most of the day despite a 530 million zloty NBP-bills sale with an overnight value date. The NBP rejected all 10 million zloty bids at its 300 million reverse repo.
